text:
sre-oncall: SLO alert -> hosted-infer gateway p99/timeouts spiked in us-west-2, 5xx fraction jumped from 0.9% to 6.2% in the last 5m. customer escalations coming in. triggering this thread to triage.

maria: seeing same in dashboards. error class is mostly 504 + upstream handshake timeouts. A few 502s too.

sam: tracing shows lots of missing spans for the inbound proxy -> batcher handoff. sampling is low for these traffic patterns. suspect prefetch handshake flaps.

sre-oncall: support reported tickets #INC-1142 and #INC-1143, both from high-traffic customers; they see client-side timeouts and retry storms.

josh: can someone paste the log query that surfaces the 5xx spike?

sam: use this in logs: ```service=gateway env=prod | where status >= 500 and region="us-west-2" | count() by status, upstream_service``` returning top upstreams: batcher-v2, kvcache, infer-proxy. latency buckets show handshake > 2s for many.

maria: I ran a quick trace coverage query: ```trace_count(service=gateway) - spans_with_parent(batch_handshake)``` -> ~40% gap on affected hosts. trace export looks truncated around the proxy->batcher boundary.

sre-oncall: infra-bot, are there any recent deploys in us-west-2?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: No gateway or batcher deploys in the last 30m. Reconciler shows a scheduled runtime config rollout completed 12m ago.

josh: rollout of runtime config = likely candidate (kv cache ttl / handshake timeout bump). rolling it back for a small canary might help.

sam: I can grep logs for the rollout id and related config key: ```grep -R "kv_prefetch_ttl" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 50``` shows repeated handshake retries after the new ttl applied.

sre-oncall: temporary mitigation: route a fraction of prod traffic in us-west-2 to fallback model variant in other AZ (us-west-2b -> us-west-2c) and enable aggressive connection pooling. I'll open a routing override.

maria: support: please reply to customers with ETA ~30m and ask them to avoid retry storms. adding note to tickets.

support: doing that now, linking incident to #INC-1142/1143. Also asked for request ids — customers provided X-Req-Ids, attaching.

josh: for root cause, we should confirm (1) trace gap due to instrumentation drop, or (2) actual handshake failures at batcher. I can run tcpdump on a problematic host for 60s.

sam: I'll prepare a short query to correlate auth token age with handshake failures: ```logs | where upstream="batcher-v2" and status==504 | parse token_age as int | histogram token_age``` — early runs show correlation with tokens rotated in last 10m.

maria: interesting — token rotations + runtime config change could cause transient auth failures leading to handshake timeouts.

sre-oncall: action items: 1) rollback runtime config canary (josh) 2) route 10% traffic to fallback AZ (oncall) 3) collect tcpdump + trace snippets (josh/sam) 4) support notify customers (support). Keep this thread updated.

sam: creating a dashboard panel for the next hour to monitor 5xx by upstream + token_age. putting link in thread: https://console.redwood/internal/d/abc123/timeout-triage

sre-oncall: update: rollback initiated (canary only). will monitor for 2 minutes.

maria: after rollback p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 320ms on the canary hosts. 5xx fraction there back to baseline.

support: customers notified, they replied that errors decreased on their end.

josh: capturing tcpdump + attaching a pcap: /var/tmp/triage_usw2_4820012345.pcap. I see repeated TLS handshake renegotiation failures with the batcher certificate during the problematic window.

maria: that matches auth token rotation + cert expiry edge-case. I'll open a postmortem ticket to cover certificate/staggered rotation and add a preflight check in the runtime rollout job.

sre-oncall: closing immediate incident — SLO trending back to normal. please add findings to incident board and keep follow-ups in eng-runtime and security for certificate/token rotations. great work. :thumbsup:
